Proposals.Text:
# Recipe Box

A small app for the recipes we cook every week: pick the week's recipes, and the shopping list writes itself.

Decided so far: a web page and a phone layout from the same code; recipes are markdown files in a folder; no accounts, one household per install.

Proposals.Text:
# Design notes

The phone layout comes first: the list is used in the store, one-handed.

Units are kept as written in the recipe; adding up happens only when the units agree.

Proposals.Text:
# Search

Search finds a recipe by its title, by an ingredient, or by a word of its method. Results come as you type, best match first.

## Rules

- A title match outranks an ingredient match, which outranks a method match.
- Search ignores case and accents.
- An empty search shows every recipe, newest first.

Applied.Outcome: The build was accepted as reported; no text change.

Replies.Text:
**Build log** (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5)

Built `src/Search.js` (the index and the ranking), `public/js/search.js` (the box and the live results) and the search page. Title, ingredient and method matches are ranked as the plan says; case and accents are folded.

Checked with `test/Search.test.js`: 14 tests, all passing, including the empty search and an accented ingredient.

Proposals.Text:
# Shopping list

The shopping list is made from the recipes picked for the week: one list per week, grouped by aisle, with each item checked off as it goes into the basket.

## What goes on it

- Every ingredient of every recipe picked for the week, added up across recipes.
- Pantry staples are on the list too, marked as staples, until the pantry is tracked.
- An item added by hand stays on the list until it is checked off.

## On the phone

The list is one screen. A tap checks an item off; a swipe removes it. Checked items drop to the bottom.

Proposals.Text:
# Quantities

When two recipes want the same ingredient, the list shows one line with the quantities added up: 200 g and 300 g make 500 g. Quantities in different units stay on two lines until the units are settled.
